title: Closed immersions of algebraic stacks: stability and topology
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let all stacks below be algebraic stacks over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. A morphism $i:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X$ is a closed immersion if every scheme base change $T\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Z\to T$ is represented by a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]; products mean 2-fibre products [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Closed immersions are preserved by arbitrary algebraic-stack base change and by composition. For every closed immersion $i$, the point-space map $|i|$ is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset and sends closed subsets to closed subsets, using [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology-flat-lfp-open]. If $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ for a field $k$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $\mathcal X$ is locally of finite type over $k$, then $\mathcal Z$ is locally of finite type over $k$ as well, where local finite type is tested on smooth scheme charts by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

proof.text: Let $a:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be arbitrary and $i:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Y$ a closed immersion. For any scheme $T\to\mathcal X$, the definition of the 2-fibre product [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] identifies $T\times_{\mathcal X}(\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Z)$ with $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Z$ over $T$: on objects one forgets the redundant $\mathcal X$-object and composes its specified isomorphism with the other one; the inverse inserts the image of the $T$-object. The latter is a scheme closed in $T$ by the hypothesis on $i$. By [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products] the 2-fibre product $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Z$ is an algebraic stack, so the projection to $\mathcal X$ is a morphism of algebraic stacks; the identification above is exactly the defining scheme test for it to be a closed immersion.

For closed immersions $i:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X$ and $j:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$, fix a scheme $T\to\mathcal Y$. Put $V=T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$, a scheme closed in $T$, and $W=V\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Z$, a scheme closed in $V$. The object-and-isomorphism definition [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] identifies $W$ with $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Z$ over $T$ by composing the specified isomorphisms. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp], $W\to V\to T$ is a scheme closed immersion. This proves the scheme test for $j\circ i$.

Fix a closed immersion $i:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X$. To show $|i|$ injective, suppose two field-valued objects $z_1,z_2$ have the same image class. By [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology], after a common field extension $L$ their images are isomorphic. Choose $x=i(z_1|_L)$ and that isomorphism. Both objects, with their isomorphisms to $x$, give $L$-points of the scheme $F=\operatorname{Spec}L\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Z$ [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. By the scheme test $F$ is closed in $\operatorname{Spec}L$, so by the affine quotient description [def-weil-closed-immersion] it is $\operatorname{Spec}(L/I)$. Its existing $L$-point forces $I=0$; thus it has just one $L$-point. The corresponding objects of its discrete groupoid are isomorphic, and projecting gives $z_1|_L\simeq z_2|_L$. Hence $z_1,z_2$ define the same point of $|\mathcal Z|$.

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $p:U\to\mathcal X$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack] and put $V=U\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Z$, with projections $r:V\to\mathcal Z$ and $h:V\to U$. The scheme test makes $h$ a scheme closed immersion. The map $r$ is a smooth surjective scheme atlas by base change and surjectivity in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. For any closed $D\subseteq|\mathcal Z|$, continuity in [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology] makes $|r|^{-1}(D)$ closed in $|V|$; the closed embedding in [def-weil-closed-immersion] makes its image under $|h|$ closed in $|U|$. We have $|p|^{-1}(|i|(D))=|h|(|r|^{-1}(D))$: the forward inclusion follows by representing a point $u$ and a point $z\in D$ over a common extension where $p(u)\simeq i(z)$, yielding an object $(u,z,\phi)$ of the 2-fibre product [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; the reverse inclusion follows from its specified isomorphism $ph\simeq ir$. The closed-subset atlas criterion [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology] now makes $|i|(D)$ closed. Taking $D=|\mathcal Z|$ gives closed image. Since $|i|$ is continuous by that same node and injective by step 3, its closedness makes its inverse on the image continuous. It is therefore a homeomorphism onto a closed subset.

proof.text: Now let $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and assume $\mathcal X$ locally of finite type over $k$. By the smooth-chart meaning in the statement, choose the atlas $U\to\mathcal X$ with $U$ locally of finite type over $k$. Again $V=U\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Z$ is a scheme closed in $U$, and $V\to\mathcal Z$ is smooth and surjective by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Cover $U$ by affines $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Over each, $V$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The images of any finite algebra-generating set of $A$ generate $A/I$ over $k$. These affines cover $V$, so $V$ is locally of finite type over $k$. This smooth surjective scheme chart of $\mathcal Z$ proves the last assertion with exactly the same chart convention; neither finite generation of $I$ nor finite presentation of $i$ is needed.
